newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Postabank shareholders absolve management over run. [CORRECTED 14:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Postabank shareholders absolve management over run. [CORRECTED 14:45 GMT]

text.p: The shareholders of Postabank, Hungary's second largest commercial bank, on Friday cleared the management of responsibility for a recent panic withdrawals by depositors and approved capital hikes worth 20 billion forints ($109.6 million).
The annual shareholders' meeting approved the board of directors' 1996 business report and reelected CEO and Chairman Gabor Princz member of the board with 99 percent of the votes.

Police are currently investigating a three-day wave of deposit withdrawals worth some 24 billion forints at the end of February, after the bank said the panic was likely to have been triggered by organised rumours.
Princz told the shareholders' annual meeting on Friday that the confidence of Postabank customers had been restored.
"The bank's situation is stable," he said.
The bank's auditor said that Postabank suffered billions of forints of losses due to the run on deposits.

"The deposit withdrawals affected the 1996 balance sheet retroactively," said Zoltan Muranyi, CEO of the accounting firm Prudentia Rt. "(The run) alerted the bank and the auditors and the (risk) reserves were substantially increased."
Postabank reduced its 1996 after-tax profit figure sharply to six million forints from some three billion forints published in a preliminary earnings report before the withdrawals.
The figure is also well below the 1995 pre-tax profit of 2.83 billion forints.
The banks said in the 1996 annual report that its risk reserves totalled 14.15 billion forints at the end of 1996, 8.32 billion forints more than at the end of 1995.
The creation of risk reserves and writing off claims boosted expenditures by 18.4 billion forints in 1996.
However, the auditor said the 1996 balance sheet was improved by the 12 billion forints guarantee, which the government granted for Postabank's assets following the depositors' run.
The National Bank of Hungary also eased Postabank's obligations for placing reserves with the central bank to help the bank recover from the damage caused by the panic.

Princz told the meeting that the bank negotiated with main shareholders, who reguaranteed the state 12-billion-forint guarantee, and also held talks with the Finance Ministry ahead of decisions on the capital hike details. (Corrects from "Princz told the meeting that the bank negotiated with main shareholders to reguarantee the state 12-billion-forint guarantee")

The bank said in its annual report that the withdrawals also broke the impetus of nine years of continuous expansion, which last year led to a rise of 109.1 billion forints in the balance sheet total to 378.7 billion forints.

However, past rapid expansion and the bank's plans to develop its services and to manage companies minority-owned by the government make it necessary for Postabank to boost its 16.45 billion forints registered capital, the bank said.
The shareholders approved Postabank's offer to investors -- mainly Hungarian companies -- to raise the bank's capital by five to 10 billion forints on June 23 and June 24.
The bank will invite 22 investors for the subscription to the new shares, at a price equivalent to their 10,000 forints face value.

The investors include the social security healthcare fund, railway company MAV, electricity supplier MVM, oil and gas company MOL, the national postal company Magyar Posta and Austria's EA Generali and Volksbank Burgenland Mitte AG.

Princz told the shareholders that SBC Warburg, commissioned by Postabank, would invite foreign investors to raise the bank's capital by a further 10 billion forints. He did not name potential investors.
The capital increase is likely to be carried out in September or October, the 1996 annual report said.
Postabank plans to float its shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange following the capital increases.

Postabank's main shareholders are the social security pension fund (25 percent), Austria's Osterreichische Postsparkasse (10 percent), the social security health care fund (10 percent), Magyar Posta Rt (seven percent), Szazhalombatta local council (six percent) and EA Generali (five percent).
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040 ($ = 182.5 Hungarian Forints)
